name: Wyoming
agency: Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT), Driver Services
permitAge: 15 (instruction permit; handbook p. 7, W.S. 31-7-110(a)); restricted permit at 14-15 for hardship cases (p. 13)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours behind the wheel, including 10 at night, certified by a parent or legal guardian (handbook p. 14)
teen.holdPermit: Learner's permit at least 10 days before the intermediate permit at 16 (WYDOT learner-permits page; not in handbook). Intermediate held 6 months (full license at 16 1/2 with driver ed) or until 17 (handbook p. 7, p. 13); it expires 30 days after the 17th birthday (p. 15)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless an exception applies (medical necessity, work, school/school activity/youth sports/religious activity, with a signed exception form); handbook p. 14. A medical emergency needs no form (WYDOT learner-permits page; W.S. 31-7-110(h)(ii)(E)); also allowed with a licensed driver 18+ (statute)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate: no more than one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family, unless accompanied by a licensed driver 18+ (handbook p. 14; WYDOT page says front seat); all occupants belted
teen.phone: Reading or sending a text while driving is banned statewide (handbook p. 89); no statewide handheld call ban, some cities ban phone use

bac.under21: 0.02 (90-day suspension first offense, 6 months second within 2 years; handbook p. 22)

notes: Handbook: 'Rules of the Road', State of Wyoming Driver License Manual 2021 (PDF dated 2021-10-19; revised for laws effective July 1, 2019 and beyond). Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers. Read in full 2026-10-09.
No Spanish manual: WYDOT says all manuals are printed only in English.

Knowledge test: given only in English (handbook p. 9; WYDOT testing page); an interpreter may be used for non-commercial written tests; oral (audio) option available. Test may be taken twice a day. Number of questions and pass mark are not stated by the handbook or WYDOT site, so exam fields stay null (commercial sites say 25 questions, 20 correct).

Speed (W.S. 31-5-301): 75 mph interstates by default, 80 where designated; 70 state highways; 65 other paved; 55 unpaved; 30 urban/residential; 20 signed school zones. Handbook p. 41 lists interstates 80/75, secondary 70, residential/business 30, school 20.
Speeding in a school or construction zone always goes on the record (W.S. 31-5-301(d)); minor speeding elsewhere may not.

Handbook p. 14 lists 'medical emergency' among the exception-form cases; the statute and the WYDOT learner-permits page say no form is needed for a medical emergency. Question wy-008 follows the statute and agency page.
Move-over law and school bus camera fines not checked; not used in questions.
